newsitem.title: USA: Jump in U.S housing starts a robust signal for Fed.
newsitem.headline: Jump in U.S housing starts a robust signal for Fed.

text.p: U.S. housing starts surged in August, climbing to their loftiest levels since March 1994, suggesting that a robust economy may indeed prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates next week, economists said.
"This is a wake-up call," said Veronika White, senior economist at First Union Corp. "Given this number the chances are greater than 50 percent for a rate hike on Tuesday."
U.S. housing jumped 4.5 percent in August to a 1.525 million annual rate against a revised 1.460 million in July, the Commerce Department reported earlier.
